title: POC Weekly Sync - Model Selection & Pinning
meeting_header: Date: 2026-05-19; Time: 15:00 PT; Duration: 45m; Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Lee (CTO, HorizonDocs), Samir Gupta (ML Eng), Olivia Park (Product)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review pilot metrics (latency, cost, quality), finalize model selection and pinning approach, and agree on rollbacks/fallbacks. Customer showed slightly higher latency on long-form document summarization; discussed quantization, KV/prefix caching, and canary pin rollout plan. Next: Redwood to run 1k-sample benchmark with pinned model and share security docs and updated pricing.
topics: Model catalog comparison: redwood variants vs open models
Version pinning strategy and canary/rollback plan
transcript:
[00:00] Liam Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we'll kick off. This is Liam from Redwood, AE, with Priya our SE. How's everyone?
[00:05] Maya Lee: Hey Liam, good thanks. Running a bit behind but ready.
[00:10] Priya Patel: Great, quick agenda: review the pilot numbers you shared, talk model selection and pinning options, then fallback/rollback strategy and next steps.
[00:18] Olivia Park: Sounds good. We want to focus on latency for our summarization flow and also the hallucination rate.
[00:24] Samir Gupta: And cost — we have a tight target for tokens per doc.
[00:28] Liam Chen: Totally. Priya, do you want to walk the numbers?
[00:32] Priya Patel: Sure. So from last week's export — you ran the sample on the 2.1M token set, right? The median p50 latency for the current pinned model, redwood-compact-v1.2, was about 420ms per 512-token chunk, p95 was 1.6s, cost roughly $0.012 per 1k tokens after batching improvements. We saw increased p95 on documents with long context due to re-encoding overhead.
[01:02] Samir Gupta: That matches our logs, though our p95s looked closer to 1.8s in prod, maybe because we have longer prompt templates.
[01:08] Priya Patel: Right, longer prompt + denser context increases KV hits. We recommended enabling prefix/KV caching for session reuse; that cut the test latency by ~25% in our bench.
[01:20] Maya Lee: Could you explain the difference between redwood-compact and redwood-standard? We saw both in the catalog but not sure about the tradeoffs.
[01:26] Priya Patel: Absolutely. redwood-compact is a lower-parameter variant optimized for latency and cost — good for short responses. redwood-standard has better long-form coherence and lower hallucination, but higher compute. There's also a quantized variant, redwood-standard-q8, that reduces memory and cost but may add some small accuracy delta.
[01:44] Olivia Park: We tested an open Llama-based model too and it was cheaper but hallucinated more, especially on legal citations.
[01:52] Liam Chen: Not surprising. Many customers trade to open models for cost but then need more prompt engineering. For HorizonDocs, accuracy on citations seems non-negotiable.
[01:59] Samir Gupta: Yeah, legal citations are a blocker — if the model invents case names that's a hard fail.
[02:04] Priya Patel: So for pinning, recommended approach: pin redwood-standard-v2.0 for critical citation flows, but set up a fallback to redwood-compact-v1.2 for throughput spikes. Canary rollouts: start with 10% traffic for 48 hours, monitor hallucination/regression metrics — we have the eval harness integration to automate checks.
[02:25] Maya Lee: If we pin to v2.0, can we still automatically fallback if latency SLO breached?
[02:29] Priya Patel: Yes. Our smart routing policies let you route by latency SLO. If p95 > configured threshold, requests can failover to the compact variant. You can also configure soft-fallbacks where we retry once with a lighter prompt.
[02:41] Olivia Park: How do rollbacks work? If we deploy v2.0 and see a quality regression on the eval set, can we rollback quickly?
[02:47] Priya Patel: Rollback is immediate — you can pin previous model version or set an automatic rollback policy tied to eval regressions. There's a short propagation window but typically < 2 minutes to revert the pin.
[02:58] Samir Gupta: Two minutes is doable. What about canary monitoring — what metrics should we look at?
[03:03] Priya Patel: Focus on hallucination rate on the citation test set, p95 latency, token cost delta, and end-to-end success rate. We'll surface these in the console per-route.
[03:12] Liam Chen: Also we'll hook the regression alerts to Slack and email for the pilot.
[03:16] Maya Lee: Cool. Regarding quantization — you mentioned q8. How much of an accuracy hit?
[03:21] Priya Patel: On our internal evals q8 had about a 1-3% drop on some NLU tasks; for citation fidelity it was closer to 2-4% depending on prompt. It's dataset dependent. For legal flows we usually recommend standard float32 for the primary path, q8 for fallback or batched offline jobs.
[03:38] Olivia Park: That matches what we saw — q8 helped cost but introduced brittle completions sometimes.
[03:44] Samir Gupta: On the caching: enabling KV cache — any infra changes? We run in Dedicated VPC.
[03:49] Priya Patel: For Dedicated or Private, KV/prefix caching is supported and requires no infra change on your side; we toggle it in the serving config. For Private on-prem we'd need a small agent but for your Dedicated pilot it's config-only.
[04:00] Maya Lee: Good. Security question: does pinning affect audit logs or KMS usage? We need clear audit trail.
[04:06] Liam Chen: Pinning is recorded in the deployment history and audit logs. All key material interacts with your configured KMS — you control keys in Private; for Dedicated we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations.
[04:17] Olivia Park: Do you have SOC 2 docs?
[04:19] Liam Chen: Yes — we'll share the security pack after this call (we'll put a link in the notes).
[04:24] Maya Lee: Great. Back to model selection: what's the recommended default for us?
[04:28] Priya Patel: Recommendation: start production pilot pinned to redwood-standard-v2.0 for citation route, with a fallback to redwood-compact-v1.2. For CLI and lower-risk routes you can use redwood-compact as primary to save cost.
[04:39] Samir Gupta: What about A/B testing between v2.0 and Anthropic-ish options? We're curious about safety tradeoffs.
[04:45] Priya Patel: You can A/B and we can instrument safety metrics. But Anthropic models may behave differently on legal phrasing. If you want, Redwood can orchestrate multi-model responses and run a reranker on top.
[04:57] Olivia Park: Are rerankers part of the platform or do we host?
[05:00] Priya Patel: Both — Redwood supports a lightweight reranker as a managed route or you can bring your own. Many customers use a small cosine/reranker for citation verification.
[05:09] Liam Chen: Okay let's dig into the specific pilot tests you asked for — Samir, you shared a sample of 1k docs that stress long context right?
[05:16] Samir Gupta: Yes, 1k long-form contracts, average 5k tokens per doc pre-truncation. We chunk into 512-token windows in our current pipeline.
[05:24] Priya Patel: For that workload we recommend two things: enable KV prefix caching to avoid re-encoding common doc preamble, and consider increasing batch sizes for throughput windows. Also try the standard model with a slightly higher context window — v2.0 has improved attention kernels for long context.
[05:38] Maya Lee: Will that change our cost profile significantly?
[05:40] Priya Patel: Slightly. The standard model increases compute, but prefix caching reduces repeated compute — net cost could be flat or slightly up depending on reuse rate. We can model it precisely in the benchmark.
[05:51] Olivia Park: Can we see an example canary rollout config?
[05:54] Priya Patel: Yes — we'll send a template. It includes percent traffic, duration, metric thresholds for auto-rollback (e.g., hallucination increase > 1.5x or p95 increase > 30%).
[06:06] Liam Chen: Quick note — the pilot also asked about model pin labeling for audit. We add pin metadata including who pinned, reason, and commit sha.
[06:14] Maya Lee: Nice. That helps compliance.
[06:16] Samir Gupta: For the benchmark you mentioned earlier — can Redwood run the 1k sample with pinned v2.0 plus fallbacks and share raw logs?
[06:24] Priya Patel: Yes, Redwood can run an internal bench with your sample (we'll use masked data unless you prefer full). We'll produce a per-route CSV with latencies, tokens, costs, and hallucination binary flags from the eval harness.
[06:36] Olivia Park: Masked data is fine for now. How long will that take?
[06:40] Priya Patel: About 48 hours to run and analyze once we get the sample and confirm pipeline settings.
[06:45] Maya Lee: Ok we'll share the sample with your SE.
[06:48] Liam Chen: We'll also prepare a pricing addon for dedicated pilot—Samir what's your committed throughput target?
[06:53] Samir Gupta: We expect ~100 requests per minute with peaks to 300 RPM during ingest windows.
[06:58] Priya Patel: For 300 RPM sustained bursts, Dedicated reserve helps. We'll model cost in the sheet; I'll include burst options.
[07:06] Olivia Park: One more thing on fallbacks: if fallback returns a shorter summary it might miss mandatory disclaimers. Can we preserve mandatory sections even if using compact?
[07:14] Priya Patel: We have structured-output support — you can enforce schema checks post-completion; if the fallback doesn't meet schema, we can trigger a retry to the original model or mark for human review.
[07:25] Samir Gupta: Good. That human-in-the-loop option is important.
[07:28] Maya Lee: Any known issues with rollbacks in Private deployments? We might eventually move to Private.
[07:34] Priya Patel: For Private on-prem, rollbacks are still supported but require you to accept the pinned image in your control plane; automatic rollback can be configured but the propagation depends on your cluster update policies. We'll share best practices for that.
[07:47] Liam Chen: Cool. Let's capture action items. But first any final questions?
[07:51] Olivia Park: Not from me.
[07:52] Maya Lee: One question — you mentioned integration with our SSO for audit links, is there any extra work?
[07:56] Liam Chen: We support SAML/SSO; it's a config item on both sides. We'll send the SSO setup checklist.
[08:03] Priya Patel: OK action items: Redwood to run the bench, share security pack, send canary template, and pricing sheet. HorizonDocs to share the 1k masked sample and confirm throughput target.
[08:15] Samir Gupta: I'll drop the sample into the secure SFTP by EOD tomorrow.
[08:20] Olivia Park: I'll review the pricing once you send it.
[08:22] Liam Chen: Great. We'll aim to have bench results in ~48 hours and follow up with a short results meeting next week.
[08:28] Priya Patel: I'll also enable prefix caching in the test env and run a quick sanity check today.
[08:33] Maya Lee: Thanks everyone.
[08:35] Liam Chen: Thanks — closing.
[08:37] [meeting end]
